overall: The AG found the Chappaquiddick committee is a public body subject to the law and violated it by failing to post notice of one meeting; the minutes and deliberation claims failed, and the minutes-request claim was untimely.

allegations.summary: Committee argued it is not a public body because it reports to the IT Manager; the AG rejected this and found it subject to the law.
allegations.key_passage: We there find that the Committee does not fit within the Connelly exception.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged deliberation outside a noticed meeting, including a 2015 phone call with a carrier representative by committee members.
allegations.key_passage: less than a quorum of the Committee took part in that call. Therefore, it was not a "meeting" subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to post notice of its meetings; website posting was not required, and the bulletin board posting was found adequate except for one meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, a quorum of the Committee participated in the August 25, 2015 meeting without posting notice. This failure violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to create minutes of its meetings; draft minutes were later shown to exist for all meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee created draft minutes of its meetings, we find no violation with respect to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that a request for minutes made in April 2016 was not fulfilled within 10 days; the complaint was filed too late.
allegations.key_passage: the present complaint was filed more than 40 days after the date of request, and we therefore decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
